newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Turmoil turns voters against main Czech parties.
newsitem.headline: Turmoil turns voters against main Czech parties.

text.p: Political turmoil in early February has cost the Czech Republic's two leading political parties ground, but narrowed the gap between them, a poll released on Monday said.

The survey of 843 Czechs conducted by state-run IVVM institute showed that Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus's Civic Democratic Party (ODS) remained the most popular, with a 24 percent rating, down from 28 percent in a January IVVM poll.
Meanwhile the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD) slipped as well, down to 21 percent from 22 percent.

IVVM said the change in preferences were a reflection of unrest stemming from strikes involving teachers and rail workers, a continuing secret service scandal, and internal disputes among CSSD members.

The poll showed that small parties had gained from dissatisfaction, with centrist coaliton member, the Christian Democratic Union (KDU-CSL), gaining three points to 14 percent, and right wing coalition member Civic Democratic Alliance (ODA) recording a 1.5 percent increase to 8.5 percent.
The extreme far-right Republicans bounced back to five percent from just one percent in January, and the little- reformed Communists had eight percent, up two points from January.
IVVM said the margin of error for small parties was +/- one to two percentage points, and +/- three points for the ODS and CSSD.
Sixteen percent of those questioned were undecided. Likely turnout in elections if they were held next week would be 64 percent, the survey said. -- Jan Lopatka, Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003
